key_insight: Splat2Act shows that a general-purpose manipulation policy can be quickly adapted to a specific home or office by turning captured scenes into a personalized simulation. This enables the robot to pick up the user’s own objects without requiring costly real-world demonstrations in every environment.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of personalizing a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policy to new, user-specific indoor scenes where direct deployment performs poorly and collecting real demonstrations is expensive and impractical.
method: Use captured real scenes to build a personalized simulation of the user’s environment.
Apply a real-to-sim-to-real pipeline to adapt a pretrained VLA manipulation policy without extensive manual data collection.
Optimize the policy for the specific placement, appearance, and geometry of objects in each deployment scene.
impact: This matters because it makes robot manipulation more practical for real homes and offices, where environments differ from training data. For AI/ML practitioners, it offers a scalable path to personalization without needing expensive per-site data collection.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: captured scene -> simulation -> personalized policy -> real-world pickup
Before/after comparison showing zero-shot failure vs adapted success
Icon set for home/office objects, robot arm, and simulation environment
Bar chart or success-rate graphic comparing generalist policy and Splat2Act
paper_title: Splat2Act: From Captured Scenes to Personalized VLA Manipulation
paper_authors: Xiaomeng Ye, Krishna Jaganathan, Gyubeum Lim, Gunjan Chhablani, Muhammad Zubair Irshad
